run.question: Can you see any issues in recent logs for traffic-manager deployment in namespace app-102b

report.summary: Yes — one error-level log line exists for the traffic-manager workload in namespace app-102b: pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-5bcwl logged {"level":"ERROR","message":"Memory alert","error":"Memory requests above 90%, consider adding more memory","status":501,"request_id":"req-a]8f2c1d4"} at 2026-11-21T05:23:31Z. It is the only ERROR line among the 151 Loki lines for the namespace in the 24h authorized window; the other 150 lines are INFO "HTTP request completed" entries (GET /health, /api/v1/orders, /api/v1/inventory, /api/v1/users, /api/v1/products; statuses 200/201/204; response_time_ms 51-199) spread 50 per pod. The workload itself looks freshly created and healthy at the object level: Deployment traffic-manager was created 2026-11-21T05:23:29Z (generation 1, revision 1, 3/3 ready/available), its single ReplicaSet scaled 0->3, and all three nginx pods are Running/Ready with restartCount 0, no previous container instance, and only plain-text nginx startup lines (23 each) in their container stdout. Important limits: because the Deployment and pods were created 11 and 9 seconds before the window end, the available log coverage is only ~50 ms at 05:23:31, and Prometheus was unavailable, so the memory claim in the error line could not be verified and no memory-pressure series was read. Net: a single error log line is the only issue visible in recent logs; that it reflects real memory pressure is an unverified hypothesis, and no root-cause object is identified.

claims.text: Deployment traffic-manager in namespace app-102b is at 3/3 replicas: spec.replicas 3, readyReplicas 3, availableReplicas 3, updatedReplicas 3, deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 1, generation 1, creationTimestamp 2026-11-21T05:23:29Z.

The traffic-manager pod template has selector matchLabels app=nginx and a single container named nginx with image nginx:latest on containerPort 80 and empty resources ({}); the running pods report qosClass BestEffort, so no memory/CPU requests or limits are defined for this workload.
Exactly one ReplicaSet exists in app-102b: traffic-manager-585c5579f6, owned by Deployment traffic-manager, creationTimestamp 2026-11-21T05:23:29Z, with readyReplicas 3 and replicas 3.

Events for the Deployment show a single scale-up at creation: Deployment traffic-manager reason ScalingReplicaSet, message "Scaled up replica set traffic-manager-585c5579f6 from 0 to 3" at 2026-11-21T05:23:29Z, plus three ReplicaSet traffic-manager-585c5579f6 SuccessfulCreate events at the same second; all 19 app-102b events in the window are type Normal (Scheduled, Pulling, Pulled, Created, Started).

All three traffic-manager pods (traffic-manager-585c5579f6-5bcwl, -9whbx, -lcr2l) are phase Running, Ready condition True, container nginx ready true, restartCount 0, lastState empty, and the log fetch reports no previous container instance (HTTP 400 previous terminated container not found) for any of them.

Each pod's nginx container stdout holds only 23 plain-text startup lines between 2026-11-21T05:23:30Z and 2026-11-21T05:23:31Z (docker-entrypoint configuration complete, "nginx/1.31.9", "start worker process 36" through "start worker process 43"); no error, failure, panic or exception line appears in any of the three containers' logs.

Loki holds 151 lines for namespace app-102b in the 24h window, all timestamped 2026-11-21T05:23:31Z: 50 INFO lines each for pods -5bcwl, -9whbx and -lcr2l, plus exactly 1 ERROR line on pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-5bcwl.

The single ERROR log line is on pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-5bcwl, container nginx, at 2026-11-21T05:23:31Z, with exact text {"level":"ERROR","message":"Memory alert","error":"Memory requests above 90%, consider adding more memory","status":501,"request_id":"req-a]8f2c1d4"}; a dedicated ERROR-filtered Loki query over the same window returned this one line only.

The remaining Loki lines are INFO "HTTP request completed" records with method GET on paths /health, /api/v1/orders, /api/v1/inventory, /api/v1/users and /api/v1/products, HTTP statuses 200/201/204 and response_time_ms values between 51 and 199.

Cluster-wide, the only pods labelled app=nginx are the three in app-102b (images nginx:latest), and the only Deployment whose name contains "traffic" is app-102b/traffic-manager, created 2026-11-21T05:23:29Z — so the queried entity is unique and no other traffic-manager deployment exists.
The only ConfigMap present in namespace app-102b is kube-root-ca.crt (key ca.crt), i.e. the namespace root CA bundle; there is no application configuration object for traffic-manager.

No crash, restart or eviction marks accompany the error line: restartCount is 0 on all three pods, every lastState is empty, no previous container exists, and the window's app-102b events contain no Unhealthy, BackOff, Evicted, OOMKilling or Killing reason for these pods.

The container stdout fetched from the kubelet for all three pods contains no ERROR or exception text at all, so the "Memory alert" line is present only in the Loki stream (labels job=nginx, service_name=nginx, container=nginx) and not in the containers' own stdout as returned by the pod log fetch.

Hypothesis (unverified): the "Memory requests above 90%, consider adding more memory" line reflects genuine memory pressure on pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-5bcwl. Countervailing evidence: the workload declares no memory request or limit (resources {}), so a 90% requests threshold cannot be computed from its configured requests, and Prometheus was unavailable to read container memory series; the message's meaning therefore remains unresolved.

Hypothesis (unverified): the ERROR line originates in the log/metric ingestion path rather than from the nginx process, since the same containers' stdout read through the kubelet contains only nginx startup text and no such JSON record; this could be a synthetic or misattributed log entry, but no evidence identifies the producer.

Rejected: that the traffic-manager pods restarted, were OOMKilled or were evicted during the window. restartCount is 0, lastState is empty, no previous container instance exists and no OOMKilled/Evicted/Unhealthy event names these pods.

Rejected: that a template-changing rollout of an existing traffic-manager deployment happened in the window. The Deployment itself was created 2026-11-21T05:23:29Z at generation 1 / revision 1, has one ReplicaSet created at that same second, and the only scale event is 0->3, so there was no older ReplicaSet being replaced.

When Prometheus is reachable, verify the memory message with container-level series (e.g. container_memory_working_set_bytes and kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total filtered to namespace=app-102b, pod=~"traffic-manager-.*") before acting on it; also consider whether a memory request/limit should be declared for this BestEffort nginx workload.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable during this Run: get_metric_names ({__name__=~"container_memory.*"} and {__name__=~"kube_pod_container.*"}), get_label_values(job) for namespace=app-102b, metrics_range_query kube_pod_owner{namespace="app-102b"} and execute_prometheus_instant_query kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="app-102b"} all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so memory usage/requests, restart counters and scrape health for the traffic-manager pods could not be checked and the "Memory requests above 90%" claim is unverified.

Log coverage for the deployment is only about 50 ms: Loki returns just 151 lines for app-102b and all are timestamped 2026-11-21T05:23:31Z, while the Deployment was created 2026-11-21T05:23:29Z and the pods started 2026-11-21T05:23:30-31Z, so nothing is known about behavior before 05:23:31 in the 24h window and "recent logs" cannot describe earlier operation.

The two log sources disagree for the same pods: the kubelet pod-log fetch returned only plain-text nginx startup lines, while Loki returned only JSON request/ERROR lines with no overlap; which one reflects the container's real stdout is unknown.

Who or what created Deployment traffic-manager at 2026-11-21T05:23:29Z, and whether it existed before that instant, is unknown: no Deployment create event was captured and the change_history integration is not integrated in this Run.

A WARN/WARNING/FATAL/CRITICAL Loki query over namespace app-102b returned nothing (no_data), and no Service or Ingress objects were returned for app-102b (both queries no_data) — these are empty query results, not verified absences, so whether the pods are exposed or reachable via any Service/Ingress is unchecked.

Events for other workloads in the window (6 Unhealthy Pod events in kube-system, 4 Unhealthy and 2 BackOff Pod events in otel-demo, 1 BackOff in local-path-storage) belong to objects outside namespace app-102b and were not investigated; they are not attributed to traffic-manager.
next_steps: Once Prometheus is reachable, query container_memory_working_set_bytes / container_memory_usage_bytes and kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total for namespace=app-102b, pod=~"traffic-manager-585c5579f6-.*" across the incident window to confirm or refute memory pressure.

Confirm with the log pipeline how the JSON ERROR record reaches Loki with container=nginx when the container stdout read via the kubelet contains only nginx startup text, and whether the "Memory alert" record is generated by the application or by the logging stack.
Check change history/audit records for the creation of Deployment traffic-manager at 2026-11-21T05:23:29Z, since that integration is not available in this Run.
Confirm whether a Service or Ingress is expected to front these app=nginx pods in app-102b, since no Service, Ingress or NetworkPolicy object was returned for the namespace.
